candidates.formal_type: (n : Nat) → Matrix.{0, 0, 0} (Fin n) (Fin n) Int → Prop

∀ (n : Nat) (adj : Matrix.{0, 0, 0} (Fin n) (Fin n) Int),
  Matrix.IsSymm.{0, 0} adj →
    (∀ (i j : Fin n), Or (Eq.{1} (adj i j) 0) (Eq.{1} (adj i j) 1)) →
      (∀ (i j : Fin n),
          Exists.{1} fun path =>
            And (Eq.{1} (List.head?.{0} path) (Option.some.{0} i))
              (And (Eq.{1} (List.getLast?.{0} path) (Option.some.{0} j))
                (∀ (k : Nat) (h : LT.lt.{0} (HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} k 1) (List.length.{0} path)),
                  Eq.{1} (adj (List.get.{0} path ⟨k, ⋯⟩) (List.get.{0} path ⟨HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} k 1, h⟩)) 1))) →
        Iff (Etingof.IsFiniteTypeQuiver n adj) (Etingof.IsDynkinDiagram n adj)

source_text:
**Problem 6.1.5.** Let $Q$ be a quiver with a set of vertices $D$. We say that $Q$ is of **finite type** if it has finitely many indecomposable representations. Let $b_{ij}$ be the number of directed edges from $i$ to $j$ in $Q$ ($i, j \in D$).

We have the following remarkable theorem, proved by P. Gabriel in the early 1970s.
